text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

The United States is keen to explore the use of bilateral free-trade agreements within the APEC region, and wants to revitalise the APEC free-trade agenda by imposing strict deadlines on working groups to come up with concrete reform initiatives, as analysts are concerned that the regional trade reform process has lost momentum and lacks direction. Page 3.

The Australian Stock Exchange's electronic share settlement system CHESS, has become involved in a scandal linked with an Adelaide stockbroker and some Adelaide clients of a financial planning business. ASX management said the investors, who collectively face losses of up to A$10 million, should be covered by the ASX's national guarantee fund. The ASX indicated an investigation in CHESS security procedures would be launched. Page 1.

Telecommunications service providers stepped up their legal wrangle with Telstra, with the providers, including AAPT, Pacific Star and First Netcom, estimating business losses of up to A$150 million a year because of the national carrier's billing inaccurcies. A survey by the Service Provider Action Network also found on-going costs associated with rectifying Telstra billing errors of A$36-A$60 million a year. Page 3.

Two bidders have been short-listed for control of Axiom Funds Management, with the National Australia Bank and German financial conglomerate Deutsche Morgan Grenfell the final contenders. The NAB's bid is believed to be a slightly higher quote, with both bids understood to be over A$200 million. Page 21.

Pacific Dunlop's purchase of US-based safety glove manufacturer Golden Needles Knitting Inc is expected to be announced today, in a deal estimated to be worth A$100 million. The new company will be an extension of Ansell's safety-glove range.

Cable & Wireless deputy chief executive Rod Olsen has confirmed the company's commitment to Optus Communications by claiming Optus has done well and is in a strong position despite the impending deregulation of the telecommunications market. Olsen does not believe Optus will be marginalised, and reinforced Cable & Wireless' belief that Optus is a core strategic investment. Cable & Wireless' holds just under 25 per cent of Optus. Page 21.
THE AUSTRALIAN

According to the latest Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics econometric study, named Gigabare, matching proposed global limits on greenhouse gas emissions could cost the Australian economy A$7,000-a-head over the 20 years to 2020 - four times as much as a 1995 study had forecast. Page 17.

In a key strategic move, the latest in a long-running internal shake-up within, Carlton & United Breweries is abolishing its 160-person purchasing department and introducing electronic purchasing of all its raw materials, with only half of the staff remaiing with the brewing giant. Page 17.

After last week posting a record net profit of NZ$60.6 million on a 7.1 per cent lift in revenue to NZ$457.9 million, thanks largely to strong growth in Australia, Government-owned Television New Zealand has revealed it is committed to expanding its presece here. TVNZ already employs 120 staff at its regional headquarters in Sydney and chief executive Chris Anderson says they are committed to boosting staff numbers in Australia. Page 17.

Speaking on the Nine Network's Business Sunday program yesterday, Wallis Committee member Jeff Carmichael hit back at criticism of the Committee's report by Commonwealth Bank managing director David Murray, who said the report's recommendations could put ustralia at risk of a US savings and loans type scandal. Carmichael said Murray's comments were "almost absurd" and accused him of scaremongering. Page 19.

French-owned wine giant Orlando Wyndham yesterday took the unusual step of complaining to its former subsidiary, Simeon Wines Ltd, that it had not received advanced notice of Simeon's intention to make a A$115 million takeover bid for fellow vintner Australian Vintage Ltd. Page 19.

According to Ricegrowers' Association executive director Mike Hedditch, this year's rice harvest, which is expected to produce a record 1.4 million tonnes and has already delivered 1 million tonnes, is way ahead of previous record deliveries in terms of rate of receival, with still another month of harvesting to go. Page 19.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

BHP is expected to announce plans tomorrow to scale-down its Newcastle steel operations as part of a far-reaching review of its steel division. Tuesday's announcement is expected to see BHP Steel slash its workforce to fewer than 900 over the next three yars as speculation mounts that BHP plans to quit the steel industry in the long term. Page 37.

Wholesale drug distributor Australian Pharmaceutical Industries is set to gain member approval for its compliance listing on the Australian Stock Exchange tomorrow. The group's 2,400-member shareholders will meet to approve the listing, paving the way fora national expansion of distribution activities. Page 37.

The Institute of Actuaries of Australia has urged the Federal Government to use an opportunity provided by the Wallis report to impose uniform capital adequacy requirements on banks and insurance companies. The IAA believes the move will provide better prtection for investors. Page 37.

The identity of the investor willing to pump A$40 million-plus into the Cairns Reef Casino Trust is expected to be formally revealed tomorrow, with the main contenders believed to be Melbourne casino owner Crown, Malaysia's Metroplex group and Queensland-ased Jupiters. Page 39.

Stockbroking analysts said yesterday that an exceptional March quarter performance by Delta Gold's 40 per cent owned Granny Smith mine in Western Australia was expected to translate into a rise in Delta Gold's share price. Page 39.

In an Industry Commission report released today claims Australia will fail to meet initial targets to reduce greenhouse gas pollution and advocates an increased role for market-based greenhouse controls. The report favours a system of tradable emission pemits over proposals for a carbon tax. The Industry Commission believes a permits-based system would force polluters to curb their activities. Page. 40.
THE AGE

The virtual closure of Newcastle operations and plans to cut up to A$500 million in costs over the next 18 months is expected to be announced when mining giant BHP reveals details from a major review of its steel division tomorrow. The Newcastle operation are tipped to be the worst affected in the wake of BHP Steel struggling to make profits following the collapse of steel-prices last year. Page B1.

Alcoa of Australia has emerged from a climate of lower alumina prices to post a first-quarter profit of A$103.59 million. The result for the three months ending 31 March is on track for an increase on the 1996 calendar year profit of A$388.3 million. WMC, holding nearly 40 per cent stake of Alcoa, last week highlighted an improved outlook for the global alumina-aluminium markets. Page B1.

Research group BIS Shrapnel claim the residential construction market has a buoyant medium-term outlook as demand for housing exceeds new construction for the first time since 1992. The group expects underlying demand for housing to jump 3 per cent to 137,400 dwellings a year for the next five years. Page B1.

A barrage of US economic statistics due out this week could weaken Australian financial markets as investors grapple with concerns over interest rates in the US and watch local data for signs of a need for a domestic rate cut. Page B3.

Exploration at the aptly named Silver Swan nickel find near Kalgoorlie, WA, continues to extend the predictions of mineral production from the A$46 million development. The US partner in the project, Pittston Mineral Ventures, claim the nickel mineralisaton has been located at a depth of 800 meters. This is an increase on the previous depth of 735 metres at Silver Swan. Page B3.

French-based wine group Orlando Wyndham is reviewing its association with its 41 per cent owned Simeon Wines after claims yesterday it was not informed about the proposed A$111 million takeover of Australian Vintage. Simeon launched the bid early last wek and plans to use the takeover as a means to expand into the domestic wine-processing industry. Page B3.
